answer: Reputation accrues like sediment in a karst cave: each honest transaction deposits a thin layer, building slowly over months. An agent silent too long sees scores whisper downward through exponential decay. To fake ten identities an attacker must age them in parallel, paying real compute and storage fees for each dormant agent while waiting for trust to harden. A gale of new registrations triggers network-wide scrutiny, quarantining young agents to low-value tasks until time proves them genuine.
